spec.name: Convoy Hauler Mk-IV 'Lockjaw'
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk six-wheeled armoured convoy hauler with a slab-sided cab, gun turret and roof rack, towing a sealed hazard-striped cargo pod on its flatbed, lit with neon trim.
spec.layout: Long chunky silhouette facing +Z. Front 0 to 4.2: a wedge-nosed armoured cab (sloped hood with a bull-bar ram and angular headlight slits, a raised cockpit with a narrow cyan-lit slit windscreen, side armour skirts, an roof turret behind the cab roof). Behind the cab, a long flatbed chassis from z=-0.6 to z=-4.2 carries a big rounded-box sealed cargo pod with chevron hazard stripes, clamp straps, a glowing magenta seam and a biohazard-style emblem decal. Six fat low-poly wheels on three axles (front z=2.7, middle z=-0.9, rear z=-3.3) with hubcaps and neon rim rings, fender arches over them. Everything is faceted and blocky: sheet-metal panels with rivet seams, dark gunmetal hull, yellow-black hazard trim, cyan and magenta neon strips and emissive glow lights, antenna masts, exhaust stacks behind the cab, tail lights red. Style shows via bold neon edge strips, decals/signage in SVG (kanji-like glyphs, serial numbers) and grime paint.

parts.attaches: Deck at chassisTop (y=1.2) carries the pod and rack; cab mounts at cabFloor; wheels pivot on axleFront/axleMid/axleRear lines.

parts.builds: Armoured cab: wedge nose with sloped hood plates, front grille with glowing cyan slits and a heavy yellow-black striped ram bar, angular headlight slits (lime/white emissive), a raised cockpit with a narrow glass slit windscreen (emissive cyan tint with SVG HUD-like glyph decal), side armour plates with rivets and door seams, wing mirrors, roof armour with vents, side-door decals (unit number, kanji-like glyphs via SVG), antenna mast with blinking red tip, neon edge strips in cyan along the roofline. Hull painted with panelled gunmetal and grime paint.
parts.attaches: Sits on chassis at cabFloor (y=1.2); roof at cabRoof; turret rides on turretRing.

parts.attaches: Base ring at turretRing (y=2.35); rack rests on chassisTop line at rackBack and cab roof.

parts.builds: Sealed cargo pod: large rounded-box capsule built from a lofted body in light podShell paint with panel seams, dark end caps, a hinged-looking lid seam on podLid, four heavy clamp straps (trim yellow/black) with bolt plates bolted to the bed, glowing magenta seam strips and a lit status screen near the front, hazard chevron stripes (SVG texture) along the flanks, a biohazard/quarantine emblem and serial number decals (SVG), rear locking wheel and cable conduits, small corner anchors. Red warning beacon on top that glows.
parts.attaches: Rests on the flatbed at podBed (y=1.3); clamps weld to the chassis deck; lid hinge at podLid.

parts.builds: Armoured side hardware and lighting along the whole hauler: left and right side armour panels between cab and pod with rivet seams, fold-down tool lockers, ladder rungs to the deck, cable runs, fuel tank cylinders under the deck edge, a neon strip loop along each flank (cyan up front, magenta at the back), floodlight pods at the cab corners, license-plate/hologram sign at the rear with an SVG glyph, bundled antenna array at the rear, spare tyre on the side, and grime/scratch paint decals.
parts.attaches: Mounted to chassis sides at chassisTop and to the pod and cab walls; does not intersect wheels at axle lines.

For decals like hazard stripes and the emblem, I'm considering building the body from a boxy core so flat side planes can be easily attached, since a rounded loft shape would complicate placing flat decal planes.

Setting the lower main box as the body and an upper box as the lid, skipping true chamfers in favor of thin corner rods for a rounded-edge look. Mapping out strap positions along the z-axis at four evenly spaced points.

Still writing shapes...

Still positioning wheel parts...

Now I'm adding mudflaps as flat boxes positioned behind the rear wheels.

I also want magenta underglow strips beneath the rails, thin emissive boxes running the length of the body, plus exhaust stacks placed behind the cab at roughly chest height on either side.

Checking the stack placement against the turret and pod boxes to make sure they don't collide — turret housing sits at x ±1.3, pod extends to z -0.7, so putting stacks at x ±1.2, z -0.05 with a small radius keeps them clear, rising from y 1.2 to 2.5 with a capped top.

Now I need rivet-panelled paint for the hull and a grime overlay — I'm defining a grime paint function that mixes the base color toward near-black using layered noise, weighted more heavily at lower elevations, and resolving the base color properly before mixing.

For the hazard stripes I'm writing a diagonal checkerboard paint function parameterized by axis so it works on both the skirt (facing x) and bumper (facing z) panels. Then I'm adding a tiny glowing neon ring on the rim, detailing the tire as a flat-shaded low-poly cylinder, and giving the sidewall a slightly raised darker inner ring before moving on to the hub geometry.

Working out hub, lug nuts, rim disc, and neon ring placement...

Now I'm placing the rear tow hook as a small torus loop near the bumper, plus red glow boxes for tail lights slightly protruding past the bumper face, and adding a front crossmember box near the bumper.

I'm laying out the ladder-frame crossmembers as merged dark boxes spaced along the chassis, checking clearance against the axle, differential housing, and rail geometry, then planning the deck as a top plate spanning the frame.

Now I'm adding deck edge trim with hazard-striped boxes along both sides, and considering a small SVG decal plate on the skirt showing an identifying marking like "LOCKJAW-04" instead of kanji text since glyph rendering may not work reliably.

Positioning the serial plate as a thin plane on the outer skirt face, with mirrored orientation on the opposite side so text reads correctly from outside. I'm also refining the skirt geometry, adding a hazard-striped trim strip along its lower edge and working out the z-range segments so the skirt clears the front and mid wheel positions properly.

Now I'm sizing the rear skirt segment to sit between the mid and rear wheel edges, and setting the skirt's height and thickness so it stays clear of the deck and wheels while keeping overall part and triangle counts reasonable. I'm also considering adding underglow strips along the skirt bottom.

Writing helper functions...

Then I'm planning the axle as a steel cylinder bridging the hubs, and the exhaust stack with rim bands, a cap, a rust-colored heat shield, and a mounting bracket — checking that the stack placement at the outer edge stays clear of the deck and skirts.

Working out the fender plate tilt direction: rotating about X by positive θ tips the +Z side downward, so I'll use +35° for the front plate and -35° for the rear to get the descending slope I want. Tire color stays flat grime tone, then I'll write it out.

spec.name: Hover Technical
spec.description: A militarized pickup truck converted to ride on four glowing hover thrusters, low-poly cyberpunk with neon trim, armor plates and a bed-mounted weapon.
spec.layout: A boxy pickup hovering about 0.45 m above the floor on four ducted thrusters that replace the wheels (one at each corner, wheel-arch positions). The front (+Z) has a sloped armored hood with a bull-bar, slit headlights and a cyan neon strip. The cab sits mid-length with a sloped windshield, side windows and a roll cage with a light bar on the roof. Behind it is an open cargo bed with a swivel gun mount, ammo crates and a rear bumper with a tail thruster. Palette is dark gunmetal hull, hazard-yellow trim, neon cyan and magenta glow on thrusters and underglow, with panelled/worn paints, decals (stripes, serial numbers, kanji/glyph signs) and glowing parts for lights, thruster cores and screens. Everything is faceted: boxes, wedges, extrudes and low-segment lathes. Only the thrusters touch no floor: the hull floats and the lowest points are the thruster bottoms at about y=0.

parts.builds: Underframe and lower hull: a slab chassis with skirt armor panels along both sides (panelled gunmetal paint, hazard-yellow stripe decals), front sloped hood with vents and a bull-bar bumper with magenta-lit slits, a rear bumper, glowing cyan underglow strips along the underside, and fender arches over each thruster position (arches only, not the thrusters). Includes the hood wedge ahead of the cab up to z=2.65 and the bed's outer side walls and tailgate from z=-0.9 to z=-2.65 (low-poly slab walls with ribbing and worn paint). Headlights as glowing warm slits, tail lights glowing red.
parts.attaches: Cab sits on cabFloor/chassisTop; bed interior and gun sit at bedFloor/gunPivot; thrusters hang from the four thruster mounts below the arches.

parts.builds: Passenger cabin from z=-0.9 to z=1.0, y=0.95..1.9: a faceted armored cab with sloped windshield and rear window (glass colour with a faint glowing HUD-glyph texture), side windows with armor slats, doors with handles and a hazard stripe, a roof with a roll-cage frame of rods, a glowing light bar (warm and cyan) across the front of the roof, a roof antenna and a small glowing sign decal with cyberpunk glyph text. Mirrors on both sides. Simple dashboard and two seat shapes visible through the glass.
parts.attaches: Rests on cabFloor / chassisTop; the hood of the chassis meets its front at z=1.0; the bed begins behind at z=-0.9.

parts.builds: Four hover thruster pods, one per thruster mount, each on its own joint: a lathe-turned faceted duct (8-sided) with a metal-dark outer shell and yellow hazard ring, a glowing cyan thrusterCore disc inside the bottom with a magenta rim ring, internal fan blades (extruded, 6 per pod), strut arms (rods and plates) connecting each pod up to the chassis arch, small exhaust fins and a glowing downward cone/glow card for the thrust. Pods are about 0.9 m wide and the bottom of each rests at y=0 to 0.02. Also a smaller tail thruster pod centred on bumperRear (rigid on body joint) with a glowing core.
parts.attaches: Each pod is centred on its thrusterXX mount and its strut meets the chassis arch underside at y=0.85; tail pod mounts at bumperRear.

parts.builds: Everything inside and above the open cargo bed between z=-2.6 and z=-0.9: bed floor with ribbed panelled plating, ammo crates (olive crate colour with stencil decals and yellow straps), a fuel drum pair, coiled cable rods, a roll bar behind the cab, and the swivel-mounted heavy weapon on gunYaw/gunPitch: pedestal, ring base, yoke, a boxy receiver with a cyan glowing energy cell, long barrel with a shroud, muzzle brake, ammo belt of small spheres/boxes feeding from a box magazine, shield plate with magenta glowing slit sight. Neon cyan strip lights on bed rails and a small holo-screen card on the gun.
parts.attaches: Floor at bedFloor (y=0.95) between the chassis side walls; gun base at gunPivot with joints gunYaw and gunPitch; roll bar leans against the rear of the cab at z=-0.9.

calls.reasoning:
I'll write the buildThrusters function using the Ctx type from the module, positioning the pods centered on the mounts at roughly x=±1.05, z=1.6/-1.5, with their base at y=0.

I'm shaping the pod geometry as lathed profiles—an outer shell wall flaring from a narrow base to a wider mid-section, plus a thin hazard-trim ring band and a magenta accent ring near the bottom, defining each as a closed outline of radius/height points to feed into the lathe builder.

I'm then adding a core glow disc, a hub cylinder, and a set of six flat horizontal fan blades, each defined by a small quadrilateral cross-section extruded along a radial direction with vertical thickness, topped off with a downward glow cone.

I'm also planning a floor-level glow ring beneath the duct (using concentric stroked rings for an alpha-cut radial effect) plus a small upward glow cone tucked inside the duct beneath the fan, and now I'm working out strut placements connecting the pod shell to the underside of the arch at inward-angled positions.

Now I'm adding a mounting plate box and small radial outer-shell fins, then moving on to designing the tail pod duct at the rear bumper, oriented horizontally along the z-axis.
